UTTARA KANDA 
CHAPTER 96 
V almiki leads Sita before Rama 
WHEN the night had passed, the great descendant of Raghu went 
to the place of sacrifice to which be had summoned all the Rishis : 
Vasishtha, Vamadeva, Javali, Kashyapa, Vishvamitra, Dirghat-
mas and Durvasa of rigid penances, also Poulastya and Shakti, 
Bhatgava, Vamana, Markandeya, Dhirghayus and the highly 
renowned Maudgalya, Garga, Chyavana, the virtuous Shatan-
anda, the far-famed Bharadwaja, the illustrious Agniputra, 
Narada, Parvata and Gautama of great glory, all these ascetics 
and others of austere observances, in great numbers. 
Inspired by curiosity, they all assembled, as also the intrepid 
titans ; and the valisnt monkeys and kings, intrigued, gathered 
there in like manner, with the warriors, merchants and thousands 
of the lower caste. Bralunins of rigid penances atrived from 
every region and all met together to be present at the taking of 
the oath by Sita ; and that immense multitude stood absolutely 
motionless, as if turned to stone. 
Knowing that all were come, the foremost of Sages immediately 
approached with Sita following him, her head bowed, her palms 
joined, choked with sobs, her mind absorbed in Rama. 
Beholding Sita walking behind Valmiki, like unto the holy 
Sbruti following in Brahma's footsteps, there arose a great 
clamour with cries of " Halahala ! " from all those who were 
oppressed with ptofound sorrow on account of the unfortunate 
princess. And some cried " Hail, 0 Rama I " and some " Hail, 
0 Sita ! " while the rest acclaimed both. Thereafter, advancing 
amidst that multitude, the foremost of the ascetics, accompanied 
by Sita, addressed Raghava, saying :-
"I am Valmiki, and here, 0 Dasarathi, is Sita of virtuous ways 
and conduct, who, on account of calumny, was abandoned near 
mine hermitage, the censure of the people having inspired thee 
with fear, 0 Virtuous One ! Sita will prove her innocence ; it 
is for thee to issue the command. These two sons of Janaki,

brief.summary_1line: Valmiki brings Sita before Rama at the sacrifice assembly so she may publicly prove her innocence before sages, kings, and the gathered world.

image_candidates.scene_text: Sita walks behind the sage Valmiki with bowed head and folded palms as a vast silent crowd of sages, kings, monkeys, and warriors watches.
The immense assembly cries out in grief and reverence as Sita appears, some shouting 'Hail Rama' and others 'Hail Sita'.
Valmiki stands before Rama in the sacrificial arena presenting Sita and declaring that she will prove her innocence before all.

deep.rich_summary: At Rama’s great sacrificial gathering, sages, kings, monkeys, titans, and people of every rank assemble to witness a decisive moment: Sita’s public oath of innocence. The immense crowd waits in tense silence until the sage Valmiki arrives, leading Sita. She walks behind him with bowed head and folded palms, overcome with grief yet inwardly fixed on Rama. The sight of the wronged queen moves the entire assembly to cries of sorrow and praise for both Rama and Sita. Valmiki then addresses Rama directly, declaring Sita’s virtue and explaining that she had been abandoned near his hermitage because of public slander. He announces that she will prove her purity and reveals that the twin boys raised in his care are Rama’s own sons. The scene prepares for a dramatic vindication of Sita before the whole world.

highlight_spans.why: Marks the Uttara Kanda setting, signaling the final phase of the epic where unresolved moral and familial tensions come to a climax.
Introduces the chapter centered on Sita’s public appearance before Rama and the court.
The chapter title foregrounds the pivotal act: Valmiki personally leading Sita before Rama for her vindication.
Opens the dramatic assembly at Rama’s sacrifice, gathering sages and beings from across the world to witness the moment.

top_scenes.scene_text: Valmiki solemnly leads the sorrowful Sita with bowed head and folded palms into a vast sacrificial arena crowded with sages, kings, monkeys, and celestial beings.
The immense assembly erupts in cries of grief and reverence as Sita appears behind Valmiki, the crowd shouting 'Halahala!' while others hail Rama and Sita.
Valmiki stands before Rama in the royal sacrificial court, declaring Sita’s purity and revealing that the twin boys raised in his hermitage are Rama’s sons.
